title: Tidy src/FsAnalyser.Core: HF-001, HF-003, HF-005, HF-006, HF-011, HF-024
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: HF-024's 'better' fix, taking total and free from one consistent source (GetDiskSpaceInformationW or FileFsFullSizeInformation), was not built; only the free > total guard was. Switching source would need re-measuring against Get-Volume, which SL-043's spike measured equal for GetDiskFreeSpaceExW and ASystemDriveScanRecordsWhatGetVolumeReports pins. A quota above the volume's free space still yields a positive but mixed figure (quota total less volume free); see follow_ups.
HF-005: I took the 'remove the field' option rather than adding links to the counters line, so the window's live counters are unchanged and WindowCases.ps1 expectations need no change.

HF-024 residual: under a per-user quota whose limit is ABOVE the volume's free space, GetDiskFreeSpaceExW's total less free is still a positive but meaningless figure (quota total minus volume free), which the free > total guard cannot catch. Taking both numbers from one quota-independent source (GetDiskSpaceInformationW's ActualTotal/ActualAvailable allocation units, or FileFsFullSizeInformation) would fix it, but needs re-measuring against Get-Volume as SL-043's spike did.

HF-024 was not reproduced on a real quota. Setting a per-user NTFS quota needs an administrator and changes volume configuration, and no named elevated operation covers it. A person could check it once by enabling a quota below the free space on a test volume and running the exe on that drive root.

HF-001: MainWindow's note still says 'This drive does not report file IDs'. With the value-based flag it can also show when only some files lacked IDs; a wording such as 'Some files on this drive have no file ID' would be more exact. Not changed, because it is App text outside the finding's fix.
